title: R15a: daemon.dispatch integration — empirical durations, capacity admission, adaptive concurrency limit, merge-pressure throttle, Jev scheduling annotation and decision-log rows, all behind existing [scheduler] modes
spec:
Why: the pure scheduling modules merged in this goal (duration, capacity, concurrency, merge_pressure, jev_sched, decision_log, sched_scorecard) are not called by the daemon yet; daemon.dispatch (orchestrator/daemon.py:660-860) still ranks with cold-start durations, fills wave_limit = min(slots, max_wave or slots) and never records why capacity or merge pressure changed a decision (AP P5, P6, P11, P13, P15; brief P14).
What (orchestrator/daemon.py dispatch path only; behaviour identical when [scheduler].mode == off; shadow logs, active applies). Tests: this repo runs unittest; every acceptance test id is a `def test_name(self)` method inside a unittest.TestCase subclass in the named file; no pytest fixtures; use the daemon test harness in tests/_harness.py.
1. Durations: durations = duration.durations_for(list(tasks.values())) computed once per dispatch; _wave_order(candidate_ids, tasks, durations) passes them to critical_path.rank; wave_row['priority'] = critical_path.explain(tid, tasks, durations) and wave_row['duration_sources'] = duration.explain_for(...) (source and n per task). Exceptions inside duration fall back to the cold-start dict with wave_row['duration_error'] set.
2. Capacity: snap = capacity.snapshot(pool, running_claude_workers(pool), inflight_claude_dispatches()); imminent = ids of queued execute tasks whose depends_on are all merged or (status done and pipeline.gated_at); admission = capacity.admit(wave_order, tasks, snap, priorities, imminent=imminent). wave_row['capacity'] = {'admit', 'deferred', 'assignments'}. In active mode candidates deferred by admit are removed from the wave and their dispatch entry reason becomes admit's reason; in shadow the row records them only.
3. Concurrency: pressure = merge_pressure.assess(); limit = concurrency.select_limit(hard_max=slots, ready_ids=candidate_ids, tasks, pairwise_rows=interference.pairwise([...candidates]), priorities, snapshot=snap, pressure=pressure, durations=durations); wave_limit = min(slots, max_wave or slots, limit['limit']) in active mode, unchanged in shadow; schedlog.append('concurrency', concurrency.log_row(limit, wave_ids)) every dispatch that had candidates.
4. Merge pressure: throttle = merge_pressure.throttle(candidate_ids, tasks, pressure['waiting'], pressure); active mode with [scheduler].merge_pressure_mode == 'throttle' removes throttle['deferred'] from the wave with dispatch reason 'merge_pressure'; wave_row['merge_pressure'] = pressure minus 'waiting' plus would_defer.
5. Jev scheduling: wave_row['jev_sched'] = jev_sched.annotate(result, pairwise_rows, tasks, goal_head=<git rev-parse goal/<parent> of the first candidate or 'main'>); when [scheduler].jev_mode == 'active' and scheduler mode == 'active', use its wave/deferred; any exception -> deterministic wave, error recorded.
6. Decision log: one decision_log.record(kind='wave', subject=goal id or first candidate, candidates=candidate_ids, hard_constraints=['depends_on', 'hard_interference', 'capacity'], deterministic={'baseline_order', 'wave', 'deferred', 'limit'}, historical={'durations': sources}, jev=jev_sched signals or None, selected=dispatched ids, rejected=deferred map, reason=joined limit reasons, mode=scheduler mode) per dispatch with candidates; one record(kind='capacity'/'concurrency'/'merge_pressure') only when that layer changed the wave in active mode.
7. New dispatch skip reasons added to the vocabulary: capacity reasons from admit (executor_capacity, cooldown, account_capacity, budget, reserved_for_critical:<id>, no_eligible_executor), 'merge_pressure', 'jev_sched'. scorecard.parallelism skip-reason tally must accept them (grep the reason set there; extend the tuple, no other scorecard change).
Safety: never dispatch more than free_slots; never dispatch a task whose depends_on are unmerged or whose spec review is pending; off mode produces byte-identical dispatch rows to today (regression test).
acceptance: tests/test_daemon.py::test_dispatch_off_mode_is_unchanged — with [scheduler].mode off no duration, capacity, concurrency, merge_pressure or jev_sched call happens and the dispatch row equals the pre-integration shape

tests/test_daemon.py::test_dispatch_shadow_records_durations_capacity_limit_and_pressure_without_applying — shadow mode: wave_row carries priority with empirical est_duration_s, duration_sources, capacity, concurrency limit, merge_pressure and jev_sched keys, first-come dispatch unchanged, a concurrency row and a wave decision row are written

tests/test_daemon.py::test_dispatch_active_applies_concurrency_limit_and_capacity_deferrals — active mode: wave_limit is the concurrency limit when below slots, a task admit deferred with reserved_for_critical is not dispatched and its dispatch entry carries that reason

tests/test_daemon.py::test_dispatch_active_merge_pressure_throttle_defers_only_coupled — saturated pressure with merge_pressure_mode throttle defers the coupled candidate with reason merge_pressure and dispatches the independent one

tests/test_daemon.py::test_dispatch_never_exceeds_free_slots_or_dependencies_under_any_mode — active mode with a limit above slots dispatches at most slots tasks and never a task with an unmerged dependency; a raising duration/jev_sched call falls back to the deterministic wave

tests/test_scorecard.py::test_parallelism_skip_reasons_accept_capacity_and_pressure_reasons — dispatch rows with reasons reserved_for_critical:T-1 and merge_pressure are tallied, not counted as unknown

constraints.interface_contract: dispatch(pool) signature unchanged; _wave_order(candidate_ids, tasks, durations=None); wave_row gains keys duration_sources, capacity, concurrency, merge_pressure, jev_sched; new schedlog file runs/sched/concurrency.jsonl; decision rows kind wave; new dispatch reasons listed in the spec; [scheduler].mode off byte-identical to today

result.summary: superseded by R15a v2 after spec review T-0649 (scheduler cfg defaults for the new keys; deferral handling on the lost-claim retry branch; scorecard skip tally counts action 'skipped'; keyword-only call example)

spec_review_risks.issue: _load_scheduler_cfg's default cfg dict (only mode/soft_conflict_policy/max_wave/stale_rebase) is never extended with defaults for the new keys the spec has dispatch() read directly (merge_pressure_mode, jev_mode, duration_mode, concurrency_mode, reserve_imminent). Any pool.toml or test fixture that omits these will KeyError the first time dispatch() indexes scheduler['merge_pressure_mode'] etc.

The spec's duration/capacity/concurrency/merge_pressure/jev layers are described as if added independently, but dispatch() already has a hard/soft-conflict wave via interference.select_wave (line 692-705) and a second interference.select_wave recompute on the competing-dispatcher retry path (line 767-786, triggered when stamp() loses a race). The spec never says whether admit/concurrency/merge_pressure/jev deferrals must be reapplied on that retry recompute, risking the 'never dispatch more than free_slots' and merge-pressure/jev safety guarantees once a claim is lost mid-wave.

Point 7 describes 'the reason set'/'the tuple' to extend for skip-reason tallying, but parallelism()'s skip tally (skips[reason] = skips.get(reason, 0) + 1, line 1567-1568) is a freeform dict with no enumerated tuple — any string is already accepted, so there is nothing to 'extend'. Separately, real dispatch rows use action='skipped' (daemon.py:713) while the tally only counts action=='skip' (scorecard.py:1565); existing unit tests mask this by hand-writing 'skip' in fixtures. The new reasons will pass the isolated unit test but will never appear in scorecard output computed from real dispatch logs, undermining the feature's stated purpose.

Spec step 3's call `concurrency.select_limit(hard_max=slots, ready_ids=candidate_ids, tasks, pairwise_rows=interference.pairwise([...candidates]), priorities, snapshot=snap, pressure=pressure, durations=durations)` places positional args (tasks, priorities) after keyword args — invalid Python syntax if transcribed literally by the executor.
